answer.original_source: NN, Inc. announcement, as relayed by finance.yahoo.com on 2026-07-01 (the article relays the company's own announcement and adds no separate origin)
answer.new_information: Reported by finance.yahoo.com on 2026-07-01: NN, Inc. said in late June 2026 that it would add 47 machine centers at its Wuxi, China plant for liquid cooling production for NVIDIA AI data center racks. NN said 100% of the new capacity was already pre-sold under multi-year, multi-product awards (party statement, undisclosed counterparties). NN targeted US$80–US$90 million of accretive new business in 2026 (party target, not a result). The article also reports NN's removal from the Russell Microcap Value Index in late June 2026, and third-party narrative and unnamed-analyst 2028 revenue and earnings projections for NN. These describe NN's supplier-side capacity and targets, not NVIDIA's own revenue, orders, supply commitments or product plans. The NVIDIA link is described in the article only as NVIDIA-related racks; no NVIDIA statement is cited.
answer.reason: Background only for NVDA. The incoming claim is a supplier's capacity expansion and self-reported pre-sold awards at NN, Inc., with counterparties and the NVIDIA relationship not disclosed. It is a conditional lead on NVIDIA's rack liquid-cooling supply chain, but it does not establish an NVIDIA sales, backlog, purchase obligation or annual business quantity. The NN targets, Russell index removal and 2028 projections concern NN and are out of scope for NVDA. No catalog question exists to update, and no admission reason applies: the item is not an NVIDIA annual quantity, major NVIDIA product milestone, policy stage or NVIDIA financing or purchase obligation. Limited use: if NVIDIA or a named customer later confirms rack volumes or the NN awards, that would be evidence for a supply-chain question.
answer.independent_judgement: The incoming claim is an NN, Inc. supplier-side announcement. It sits in NVIDIA's AI rack supply chain but does not carry NVIDIA's own figures, commitments or confirmation, and no NVDA question in the catalog is supplied to absorb it. The pre-sold status and the 2026 US$80–US$90 million target are NN's statements about its own business. Their relevance to NVDA is conditional on the awards and volumes being tied to NVIDIA-purchased racks, which the text does not establish. Independent sources: the identified origin is NN's own announcement; the publisher relays it and does not corroborate it.
